subject.title: feat: provider fallback by failure class — quarantine auth-broken providers

question: What default provider/profile incident policy should OpenClaw use for hard auth failures versus transient 401s, and what redacted status surface should expose it?
rationale: Current main can classify several failure classes, but choosing when auth becomes a default quarantine, when to retry same-key transient 401s, and what status fields are safe to expose changes provider routing, session behavior, and operator diagnostics.

options.title: Default incident-health model
options.body: Implement default hard-auth quarantine only after a documented confirmation boundary, preserve transient 401 recovery, and add redacted status/doctor visibility.

options.title: Keep opt-in skip only
options.body: Leave default fallback behavior unchanged and only improve operator guidance/status, accepting continued repeated attempts unless operators set the skip TTL.

options.title: Split restart subcase first
options.body: Track the config-write restart loop as a narrower repair before deciding broader provider quarantine policy.

recommendation.title: Default incident-health model
recommendation.body: Implement default hard-auth quarantine only after a documented confirmation boundary, preserve transient 401 recovery, and add redacted status/doctor visibility.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans auth runtime, provider routing, gateway status, and operator UX, where recent history shows steipete touching adjacent fallback/auth behavior.
